_doc: Curation for tools/build-photos.mjs. Keys are atomic numbers as strings. A value of null forces 'no photograph' for that element (the app shows the Bohr model). An object replaces the automatic pick: 'file' is the exact Commons title including the 'File:' prefix (its license is still checked and must be free), 'kind' is one of sample, tube, crystal, other, and 'focus' is the crop anchor for the 160x160 tile: center, top, bottom, left or right (default: sharp's attention strategy). Keys starting with an underscore are ignored.

_notes.8: Was a discharge tube (Oxygen discharge tube.jpg). Now liquid oxygen, pale blue in a beaker (Staff Sgt. Nika Glover, U.S. Air Force, public domain, 1024x1280).
_notes.9: Was Liquid fluorine tighter crop.jpg, 373x305 and blurry. Now liquid fluorine, yellow in a test tube at -196 C (Fulvio314, CC BY-SA 3.0, 1200x1673); the liquid sits in the lower half, so the tile crops to the bottom.
_notes.16: Was a native sulfur mineral specimen from a Bolivian mine. Now refined sulfur chunks on white (Ben Mills, public domain, 1925x1444).
_notes.19: Was K crystal.jpg, an unverified close-up inside an ampoule. Now freshly cut potassium pieces, silvery (Dnn87, CC BY 3.0, 4000x3000).
_notes.26: Alchemist-hp's electrolytic iron with the 1 cm3 cube, FAL. Same as the automatic pick; kept here as the verified example of the shape.
_notes.33: Was Arsen 1.jpg, 297x500, a mineral-looking specimen in a tube. Now metallic arsenic lumps in a sealed ampoule from the Hi-Res Images of Chemical Elements set (CC BY 3.0, 720x720).
_notes.53: Was Sample of iodine.jpg, a dark and blurry pile. Now a sharp pile of iodine crystals on white (Benjah-bmm27, public domain, 2021x1516).
_notes.57: Was Lanthan prvek.jpg, a hand-held vial of powder in a lab, unverified. Now a 1 cm piece of pure lanthanum in an ampoule (Jurii, CC BY 3.0, 708x708).
_notes.58: Was CE2k2g.jpg, 400x219. Now a 1 cm piece of cerium in an ampoule (Jurii, CC BY 3.0, 676x676).
_notes.59: Was Praseodym 1.jpg, 352x500. Now praseodymium metal pieces in a sealed ampoule, Hi-Res Images of Chemical Elements (CC BY 3.0, 932x932).
_notes.60: Was Neodym 1.jpg, 431x500. Now a cut neodymium block in a sealed ampoule, Hi-Res Images of Chemical Elements (CC BY 3.0, 782x782).
_notes.65: Was Terbium element.jpg, 667x500. Now a terbium lump on white, Hi-Res Images of Chemical Elements (CC BY 3.0, 704x704).
_notes.66: Was Dysprosium1.jpg, 667x500. Now a dendritic dysprosium piece, Hi-Res Images of Chemical Elements (CC BY 3.0, 1208x1208).
_notes.67: Was Holmium.jpg, 667x500. Now a dendritic ultrapure holmium piece, Hi-Res Images of Chemical Elements (CC BY 3.0, 1068x1068).
_notes.78: Was Platinum-nugget.jpg, a native nugget. Now crystals of pure platinum grown by gas-phase transport (Periodictableru, CC BY 3.0, 2084x1460).
_notes.80: Was a 1955 archival photograph of mercury drops, unverified category fallback. Now liquid mercury being poured into a dish (Bionerd, CC BY 3.0, 1209x1311).
_notes.81: Was Thallium sample.jpg, a tiny ampoule under water where the metal is barely visible. Now a close-up of 8 g of thallium under argon, Hi-Res Images of Chemical Elements (CC BY 3.0, 800x800).
_notes.86: Wikidata's image for radon is a water apparatus in a hotel dining hall, not the element. Radon is an invisible gas; Commons has no photograph of it.
_notes.87: Wikidata's image for francium is a vial of uranium mineral that contains francium only as trace decay atoms. Not a photograph of the element.
_notes.92: Was Metallic Uranium.jpg (a small bar in an ampoule on graph paper, verified but tiny in the frame). Now a billet of highly enriched uranium in gloved hands, Y-12 (U.S. DOE, public domain, 3200x2560).
_notes.100: Commons' only fermium image is an alloy carrying 0.00004 % fermium by weight: not a photograph of the element. Forced null; the Bohr model stands in.
